newsitem.title: UK: LIFFE Aug white sugar pushes higher on supply fear.
newsitem.headline: LIFFE Aug white sugar pushes higher on supply fear.

text.p: White sugar futures got off to a flying start on Monday with plenty of buying interest in the spot August contract and solid early volume, traders said.
A mixed bag of broker, commission and trade buyers pushed August up to an intraday high of $315.10, nearly $2.00 up on Friday's close.
"August is very popular all of a sudden and seems to have many friends -- they're expecting a shortage of sugar," said one trader.
August is a time of seasonal tightness as sugar from the European Union's new crop has yet to appear on the market and traders have to rely on the tail-end of the current crop for their supplies.
The spot position's bullish performance attracted buying further down the board as October and December also pushed higher by around $1.00. The December/March spread traded at $1.00.
At 1105 GMT August was up $1.20 at $314.50 and October was up $1.00 at $3104.00. Market volume was dominated by August trades and amounted to 790 lots, which traders said was encouraging.
Technical analysts pegged nearby resistance points at $313.90 and April's peak at $317.50, noting good underlying support from longer-term moving averages.
But volume on the Paris market remained light at just 67 lots. August was up $1.70 at $315.00 and October was untraded.
